name: Jump Lunge
description: The jump lunge is a plyometric exercise in which the lifter starts in a lunge position and explosively jumps into the air, switching the position of the feet mid-air to land in a lunge on the opposite leg. It trains explosive hip and knee extension power, cardiovascular conditioning, and single-leg landing mechanics. The continuous alternating nature makes it one of the most demanding bodyweight lower body exercises.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a lunge position with one foot forward and the rear knee just above the floor. Arms are bent at the sides or in running position.
execution.setup_instructions: Ensure adequate ceiling height and clear landing space. Master the stationary lunge before progressing to the jump lunge.
steps: Step 1: Start in the bottom of a lunge with one foot forward, back knee near the floor.
Step 2: Swing the arms explosively and drive through both feet to jump vertically off the ground.
Step 3: While airborne, switch the position of the legs so that the previously rear leg is now forward.
Step 4: Land softly by absorbing through the toes, then ball of foot, then heel — landing back in a lunge position.
Step 5: Immediately upon landing, absorb and spring back up into the next jump.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe rhythmically — exhale sharply at takeoff, inhale during flight, absorb on landing.
common_mistakes: Landing stiff-legged instead of absorbing through the hip and knee — high injury risk
Landing with the feet too close together, reducing stability
Using too shallow a lunge on landing, reducing the eccentric braking benefit
safety_considerations: Land softly — impact forces during plyometric landing can be 3–5 times bodyweight
Develop adequate single-leg strength before performing jump lunges
Avoid on hard surfaces — rubber flooring or grass is preferable
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lunge depth at both takeoff and landing should be near the bottom of a standard lunge.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Performed for time (20–60 seconds) or for reps with maximal effort on each jump
coaching_cues: Use your arms — they help drive the jump height
Land soft like a feather — quiet feet
Deep lunge on landing before you launch again
